name: Wang Weifeng
current_role: Former Chairman & GM of Jiangsu Zhongli Group (002309.SZ); no longer listed in its management after Xiamen C&D (建发股份) took control. Current role not found.
profile: Wang Weifeng (王伟峰), son of founder Wang Boxing, helped run Jiangsu Zhongli Group, a Changshu maker of specialty cables and solar (Tenghui PV) products; he was GM from 2019 and chairman from Aug 2022. Zhongli is now a subsidiary of state-linked Xiamen C&D, chaired by Zhuang Yu'an, and Wang no longer appears among its officers.
interesting_fact: Zhongli, founded in 1988, grew from communication/specialty cables into solar via its Tenghui (腾晖) PV subsidiary; it now sells cables to rail, marine, mining and new-energy markets in 80+ countries.
deep_cut_fact: He studied for his undergraduate degree at York University (Canada) and later earned an MBA from Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
notes: Family lost control of Zhongli in a restructuring (now controlled by Xiamen C&D, 600153.SH); avoid financial topics. No published personal contact found. Education detail from aggregator (MarketScreener); verify before use. Hurun pairs him with father Wang Boxing.

name: Alisa Moussaieff
profile: Austrian-born Alisa Moussaieff heads Moussaieff Jewellers, the London high-jewellery house she built with her husband Shlomo Moussaieff (d. 2015), known for rare coloured diamonds. She runs it with her daughters, with salons in London, Geneva and Hong Kong, and is regarded as a doyenne of the coloured-diamond trade.
interesting_fact: She married Shlomo Moussaieff in Jerusalem in 1948, two weeks before he was taken captive for a year during the Arab-Israeli war; together they built a gem business and he amassed one of the largest private collections of Biblical-era antiquities (~60,000 artefacts).
deep_cut_fact: Jewellery historian Vivienne Becker traces the Moussaieff family's gem-dealing lineage roughly 800 years back to Bukhara, the Silk Road city of gem merchants; Becker called Alisa the 'matriarch' of the global diamond industry.
notes: Very private; seldom seeks publicity (per Phillips). Best route is the house's published press contact. She is likely in her 90s; no death report found, but confirm before outreach. Mother of Dorrit Moussaieff (former First Lady of Iceland).

name: Andrew T. Kaplan
current_role: Partner (Healthcare), Bain Capital Private Equity, Boston; Director, Kailera Therapeutics (KLRA)
profile: Andrew Kaplan is a Bain Capital healthcare partner (joined 2009, ex-Goldman Sachs banker) who joined the board of obesity-drug developer Kailera Therapeutics with its $600m Series B in Oct 2025. The SEC '10% owner' holdings attributed to him reflect Bain Capital fund stakes in Kailera, not necessarily personal wealth.
interesting_fact: Kailera was launched in 2024 with $400m to develop GLP-1/GIP obesity drugs in-licensed from China's Jiangsu Hengrui, which took a 19.9% stake; it later went public as KLRA.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded EngagedHealth, LLC, a post-hospitalization service for chronically ill, low-income patients aimed at cutting readmissions; he was a Baker Scholar at Harvard Business School and studied economics at Wharton.

public_contacts.value: Kailera media/IR: maura.gavaghan@kailera.com (Maura Gavaghan, VP Corp Comms & IR, as of Oct 2024)

notes: Net worth figure is an artifact of SEC Form 4 aggregation of Bain Capital fund holdings; he is a PE partner, not a founder billionaire. Middle initial 'T.' not confirmed on Bain's page; distinct from Andrew Gary Kaplan (another Bain director). Best route: Bain Capital media office.

name: Qian Sujin
current_role: Co-founder and largest individual shareholder (5.21%) of Beijing E-Techstar Co., Ltd. (恒实科技, 300513.SZ); no longer chairman
profile: Qian Sujin (钱苏晋) co-founded Beijing E-Techstar (北京恒泰实达) in 2000 and long served as chairman/GM, building it into a digital-energy and IoT solutions provider for power grids, telecoms and smart cities, listed in Shenzhen in 2016. Kang Jinsheng now chairs the company; Qian remains a co-controlling shareholder with Zhang Xiaohong.
interesting_fact: E-Techstar's core business is digitising the power grid and telecom networks: big-data/IoT platforms for utilities, plus smart-energy, smart-city and smart-transport applications - squarely in the energy-data space.

public_contacts.value: huangzijian@techstar.com.cn (board secretary Huang Zijian, company IR contact)

notes: Hurun pairs him with Zhang Xiaohong (co-controller). Wealth now much reduced vs. 2016 listing (5.21% stake, Q3 2026). Relevant to energy/grid-digitisation theme. Low public profile; English-language coverage minimal. Web search budget ran out, so no deep-cut fact was found.

name: Shao Jianming
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Highsun Group Co., Ltd. (海印股份; reappointed March 2025)
profile: Shao Jianming (邵建明) founded Guangzhou's Highsun (海印) group in 1991, growing it from a leasing business into theme malls, wholesale markets, shopping centres and urban complexes, with a later push into finance (payments, a rural-bank stake, Huacheng Bank). He is a co-controller with Shao Jianjia (president) and Shao Jiancong.
interesting_fact: Highsun was one of the few privately controlled commercial-property companies listed in Guangzhou (Shenzhen listing 2008) and pioneered themed specialist malls in the city; it also helped found Huacheng Bank (花城银行).
deep_cut_fact: He served as a non-executive director of Guangzhou Rural Commercial Bank from 2009 to 2019.
notes: Company now trades on the NEEQ delisted-securities board ('海印5') and faces regulatory/financial issues; avoid financial topics. Deep-cut fact comes from an aggregator (MarketScreener), so verify it. Not a natural fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Xu Xiaoguang
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Xiamen Hexing Packaging Printing Co., Ltd. (合兴包装, 002228.SZ)
profile: Xu Xiaoguang (许晓光, b. 1967, MBA) has led Xiamen Hexing Packaging since 2007, building one of China's largest corrugated-carton and packaging-solutions groups (listed 2008). He and family members (Lv Xiuying, Xu Xiaorong, Xu Tianjin) are the controlling holders via Xinjiang Xinghuiju.
interesting_fact: Hexing supplies corrugated boxes and integrated packaging services to big consumer and electronics brands across China, and he has chaired it continuously since January 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Before packaging, he worked as a forecaster (预报员) at the Civil Aviation Administration of China's Xiamen air-traffic-control station, then ran Lianyu Packaging Industry Co.
notes: Resume taken from the company's filed officer bio (via Eastmoney F10). Best route is the IR department.

name: Zhang Hongbao
current_role: Major shareholder (~4.6%) of Zhejiang Dehong Automotive Electronic & Electrical (德宏股份, 603701.SH); not an officer. Control passed to Ningbo Zhenhai state investor.
profile: Zhang Hongbao (张宏保) is a founder/former controlling shareholder of Huzhou-based Zhejiang Dehong, which makes automotive alternators and electrical parts and listed in Shanghai in 2016. Control has since moved to Ningbo Zhenhai Investment (state-owned), chaired by Qin Xunyang; Zhang remains a 5%-range shareholder and has been selling down.
interesting_fact: Dehong is a specialist maker of vehicle alternators and voltage regulators, a niche supplier to Chinese commercial-vehicle and engine makers.

public_contacts.value: investor@dehong.com.cn (company IR; he is no longer management)

notes: Hurun pairs him with Zhang Liyuan (also a large holder). No personal public channel found; company IR is only an indirect route. Web search budget ran out, so no deep-cut fact was found.

name: Huo Dongling
current_role: Chairman & Executive Director, Comba Telecom Systems Holdings (2342.HK)
profile: Huo Dongling (霍东龄, known in HK as Tony Fok Tung Ling, aged 69) co-founded Guangzhou-based Comba Telecom in 1997 after years trading telecom equipment; it became a major global supplier of base-station antennas, wireless access and DAS/indoor-coverage systems for mobile operators. He still chairs the board and leads group strategy.
interesting_fact: He was named Hong Kong CEO of the Year at the CNBC Asia Business Leader Awards 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as a technical engineer (1982-87) at the Guangdong Post & Telecom Bureau's Microwave Telecommunications Main Station, and graduated in microwave communications from the Beijing Institute of Posts and Telecommunications in 1986.
notes: Hurun pairs him with Chen Jingna. Uses the English name Fok Tung Ling in HKEX filings. Telecom-infrastructure angle (5G/Open RAN) fits a data/energy-infrastructure podcast. No published IR email found on the site; HKEX annual reports list company secretary contacts.

name: James Benamor
current_role: Founder of Richmond Group (Bournemouth); former founder and controlling shareholder of Amigo Holdings. Current activities not confirmed.
profile: Bournemouth-born James Benamor (b. 1977) started loan broker Richmond Group in 1999 aged 21 and in 2005 founded guarantor lender Amigo, which floated in London in 2018 at a £1.3bn valuation. He left Amigo's board in 2020, after which Richmond Group sold its stake.
interesting_fact: Richmond Group was named one of the Sunday Times 100 Best Small Companies to Work For in 2008-2010, and Benamor won an EY Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Unable to afford advertising when he launched Richmond Group, he printed leaflets and delivered them on foot, walking about 300 km and posting 30,000 leaflets in the first month.
notes: Sensitive history: Amigo was wound down after FCA affordability issues and his 2020 public fight with Amigo's board; avoid these topics. No published contact found (web search budget ran out); Richmond Group's website would be the route to check.
